correctness.rationale: Exact symmetric-Laplacian eigenvector equations (1), discriminant and difference-factor checks exhaust all eigenvalues. At eigenvalue two, invisible modes are the cycle space of the unactuated inserted-edge subgraph, with p=q=2 handled separately. For balanced p=q, an original-only eigenvector forces an original actuator. At every spanning-tree complement, contrast eigenvectors are detected: unbalanced, two unobserved same-side labels give a forbidden K2,2 in the tree; balanced, the controlled-edge components have constrained sizes and at most one invisible contrast, killed by any original actuator. Every forest extends to a tree. Counts follow via matrix-tree theorem; verify.py replay passed 734 supplementary rank checks. No numerical experiment substitutes for proof.

value.rationale: The objective is a structural, network-control design problem with physically restricted coordinate actuators. The result classifies all admissible placements and exact minimum size for every rectangular complete-bipartite subdivision. The balanced-versus-unbalanced resonance forces an additional original actuator, which cannot be inferred from generic maximum multiplicity alone. Counting p^(q-1) q^(p-1) tree-complement placements (and balanced factor 2p) quantifies feasible equally sparse designs. It is a natural complete classification, not an arbitrary finite example or routine parameter substitution.
